title: High pick and roll
goal: A practitioner can read this play at a glance: High pick and roll.

rubric.must: The named scenario is visibly identified and its primary subject is clearly shown.
The picture visibly uses the required standard diagram structure and connected elements.
A reader can visually follow the principal flow or relationship from beginning to end.
Key labels remain legible and attached to the correct visible elements.
Lines and symbols do not visually imply unintended connections.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the playbook/basketball exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing clearly presents a complete high pick-and-roll: player 5 screens for ball-handler 1, 1 dribbles around the screen, 5 rolls toward the basket, a dashed pocket pass reaches the roll path, and the final shot points to the rim. Player 3’s corner cut and man-defense markers are also visible without materially misleading connections.

items.evidence: The title “High Pick and Roll” is prominent, and the central screen, roll, pocket pass, and shot sequence visibly depicts that play.
A recognizable half-court diagram uses numbered offense circles, red defense X marks, a ball marker, screen symbol, dribble path, cut arrows, dashed pass, shot arrow, and a legend.
The flow can be followed from player 1 and the ball, through the dribble around player 5’s screen, into the pocket pass, player 5’s roll, and the shot at the rim.
The title and key labels “Screen,” “Roll,” “Pocket pass,” and “Shot” are legible and placed beside their corresponding visible actions.
Distinct line styles separate dribbling, passing, player movement, screening, and shooting; their endpoints and arrow directions do not visibly imply an unintended play connection.
